Counsel for Applicant :- Neeraj Rastogi,Anoop Kumar,Sandeep Kumar Srivastava,Sudhaker Pr

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anand Singh Sant,Vijay Prakash Tripathi,Vivek Chauhan
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. None appears on behalf of the respondent no.2 despite service of notice.
3.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today, is taken on record.

4. In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that the informant went to stay with her parents at Delhi and for the last one year she met with the applicant and made physical relations and a video was made.
Subsequently, after five months, when the victim came back with the family, the applicant started blackmailing her.

In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she met the applicant at Delhi and they started talking with each other.
She also stated that the applicant arranged a work for her.
The victim further stated that after administering some intoxicated thing, the applicant formed physical relations and video was also made which was later uploaded on facebook and on Instagram.

A similar statement was also given under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
5.

Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that as per the school leaving certificate, date of birth of the victim is 12.2.2006 as such the victim was approximately 17 years at the time of the alleged incident.

6. In the rejoinder affidavit, learned counsel for the applicant has denied the averments made in the counter affidavit stating therein that none of the alleged videos were uploaded from the mobile of the applicant.
7. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail.
8. Considering the aforesaid submissions, prima facie it appears that the physical relations were formed by consent and continued over a period of one year.

The age determination and the uploading of the videos is to be decided at the time of the trial as in view of the rival submissions, no opinion can be expressed in respect of that aspect of the matter.
9.

Considering the fact that there is no concrete document to categorical determine the age of the victim at this stage, however there is no denial of the fact that physical relations were made which continued for a substantial time, as such the applicant who is in custody since 2.8..2023 and has no criminal history and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail,
would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity.
10.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant Ravindra Kumar Mandal @ Ravindra be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.136 of 2023, under Sections 506, 376, 509 I.P.C. and Section 67, 67-A of the Information Technology Act and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Raheemabad, District Lucknow on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
